subject: Boundary confirmation for external penetration test: managed control plane vs customer datastores
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@acme.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 16:03:00 -0400
Subject: Pen test scope clarification — Acme external assessment

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the earlier onboarding call. As part of Acme's external security assessment we need to confirm the exact boundary Redwood will include in your penetration test report you provide to customers. Specifically:

- Will Redwood's pen test/report cover the managed control plane (authentication, model serving endpoints, control plane APIs) for Hosted and Dedicated offerings?
- For Dedicated deployments where the serving instances are provisioned by Redwood but the customer data resides in a customer VPC (S3-compatible storage or DB), is the customer-managed datastore in-scope for Redwood's report, or out-of-scope?
- For Redwood Private/on-prem installations, do you provide any assessment artifacts at all or is that fully responsibility of the customer's own assessment?

We need this clarified so we can record the scope in our SIG and CAIQ responses and schedule any follow-ups. Also, can you attach the most recent pen test report and a brief asset inventory that maps which endpoints are Redwood-managed vs customer-managed?

Appreciate a short, clear response we can attach to our questionnaire.

Thanks,
Oliver Grant
Head of Security Ops — Acme Corp
security@acme.com

[Attachment requested: latest pen test report, asset mapping CSV]
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Pen test scope clarification — Acme external assessment

Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front, details below and attached.

Summary:
- Hosted (Redwood API): Our pen test covers Redwood-managed control plane and data flow that traverses Redwood infrastructure (authentication, API endpoints, model serving, runtime GPUs, and our internal logging/observability paths). Customer data stored in customer-managed external storage (e.g., your VPC buckets) is out of scope unless you ask us to include that integration point and provide access for testing.
- Dedicated (Reserved capacity): If the Dedicated pool is fully managed by Redwood (we provision and operate the serving nodes in our environment) then those serving nodes and network interfaces we control are in-scope. Any storage or compute that lives inside the customer's VPC and is managed by the customer (for example, customer-owned buckets, DBs, or on-prem GPUs) is out-of-scope for Redwood's pen test.
- Private / On-prem: For Private deployments (customer-managed control plane or on-prem package), Redwood does not perform tests on customer-controlled infrastructure by default. We can provide guidance, our internal pen-test findings for the components we ship, and a checklist of controls; if you want a Redwood-conducted assessment on your private infra we can run a jointly scoped engagement as a paid service.

Attachments included: Redwood-PT-Summary-2026-04.pdf (high-level findings and ATO status) and a shorthand asset mapping (see asset_inventory_for_acme.csv attached in my follow-up).

A couple of clarifications that are often helpful:
- "In-scope" means the component is under Redwood operational control and we will provide findings and (where applicable) remediation verification.
- Integrations (webhooks, S3, VPC peering) are typically considered out-of-scope for Redwood unless you explicitly request Redwood to coordinate testing with your team and give us access/consent.

If you share the SIG/CAIQ questions you want to mark as "Redwood-provided evidence", I can point to the exact artifacts and mark the fields accordingly. If it helps, we can provide a simple diagram that labels each endpoint as Redwood-managed vs customer-managed — I can get that to you by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Security Partnerships, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

[Attachment: Redwood-PT-Summary-2026-04.pdf]
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@acme.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 08:15:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Pen test scope clarification — Acme external assessment

Thanks Stephanie — that helps. A few follow-ups so we can close out the SIG: 

1) Can you explicitly list the public endpoints (FQDNs/IP ranges) and the authentication token endpoints that you consider Redwood-managed for Hosted and Dedicated? Our external tester needs the exact targets.
2) We have an outstanding finding from our last integration test (session fixation on the webhook retry path) — can you confirm whether that webhook retry flow (from Redwood to customer endpoint) was covered in your last report? If not, can you provide remediation status and an anticipated completion date?
3) For Dedicated customers who elect to terminate TLS at their VPC load balancer, does Redwood still run any internal tests on the application layer for the serving nodes?

Procurement is asking for the pen test artifact to live in our vendor evidence folder. Can you include a short statement we can upload that says: "Redwood Inference penetration test covers Redwood-managed control plane and serving nodes; customer-managed datastores and private infra are out-of-scope unless explicitly requested" with your signature?

We've pasted a link to our SIG/CAIQ in case you want to answer inline: https://acme-secure.com/sig/ACME-2026-pt.

Oliver

[Referenced: SIG questionnaire link]
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 09:35:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Pen test scope clarification — Acme external assessment

Oliver — thanks, noted. Below is a concise package and a proposed mutual action plan so Procurement and your security reviewer can close the SIG entry.

Evidence statement (copy-paste friendly):
"Redwood Inference penetration testing covers Redwood-managed control plane (authentication, API endpoints, model serving runtime) and Redwood-operated serving nodes. Customer-managed datastores (customer VPC buckets, customer DBs) and customer-controlled on-prem/private infra are out-of-scope for Redwood's standard penetration test reports unless explicitly included via a joint scoping agreement"

Public endpoints / targets: (high level)
- api.redwood.com (Hosted control plane API)
- *.dedicated.redwood.com (customer-dedicated endpoints hosted in Redwood-managed pools)
- auth.redwood.com (token service)
- Note: we will provide a precise IP range list and FQDNs in the asset_inventory_for_acme.csv attached to this message.

Session fixation / webhook retry flow:
- Our April 2026 engagement did not exercise customer-side webhook endpoints (those are outbound calls from Redwood to customer systems) — those remain out-of-scope unless you grant testing access.
- The retry logic server-side (Redwood's enqueue/dequeue and replay logic) was audited; there was one mid-severity finding from 2026-04 that our runtime team has remediated as of 2026-05-05. I have Rishi on copy to confirm closure; remediation notes are included in Redwood-PT-Summary-2026-04.pdf.

Dedicated TLS termination and app-layer tests:
- If TLS termination is handled at the customer's LB in their VPC, Redwood's standard pen test will not be able to test the plaintext application layer inside your VPC. We will test upstream of termination and can run additional app-layer tests if you provide scoped access.

Mutual action plan / next steps:
1) I will attach the asset_inventory_for_acme.csv and a scope diagram (pt-scope-diagram.png) that label in-scope endpoints by May 13 COB.
2) Rishi will confirm remediation evidence for the webhook-related finding and provide a short remediation write-up (by May 18).
3) If you want redrawn SIG/CAIQ answers marked "Redwood-evidence", send the specific question IDs and we will respond inline within 3 business days.
4) For Dedicated/included private testing, if you want Redwood to extend scope into your VPC or on-prem hosts we can draft a joint scoping statement and quote the engagement; procurement can coordinate with Monica for pricing and SOW.

Attachments: asset_inventory_for_acme.csv (endpoint/FQDN list + IP ranges), pt-scope-diagram.png, Redwood-PT-Summary-2026-04.pdf

If that works, I'll upload the one-paragraph evidence statement to your vendor portal for Procurement as well.

Thanks — Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Security Partnerships, Redwood Inference
